title: Vertex Algebra Axioms and State–Field Constructions

items.title: Formal distributions and fields on a vector space
items.statement: Define two-variable formal distributions with coefficientwise polynomial multiplication, residues, the formal delta function, the two binomial expansion conventions, and an End(V)-valued field by its lower-truncation property on every vector.

items.title: The affine vacuum character exists at every complex level
items.statement: For every k in C, the assignment g[t] -> 0 and K -> k defines a one-dimensional representation of g[t] plus CK.

items.title: Vertex algebra in the state–field convention
items.statement: Define a complex vector space with nonzero vacuum, translation operator T, and state-field map Y(a,z)=sum a_(n) z^(-n-1), requiring lower truncation, vacuum and creation identities, translation covariance, and pairwise locality.

items.title: Universal affine vacuum module
items.statement: For finite-dimensional complex simple g with the normalized form and k in C, define V^k(g)=U(ghat) tensor over U(g[t] plus CK) C_k, with g[t] killing the vacuum and K acting by k; include the absence of the degree derivation.

items.title: Locality determines the formal OPE coefficients
items.statement: For mutually local fields A(z), B(w), prove the finite delta-derivative commutator expansion, its residue formula for coefficients, the OPE singular-part expansion, and the induced mode commutator identity including generalized binomial coefficients.

items.title: PBW basis of the universal affine vacuum module
items.statement: Prove for the countably based affine Lie algebra that the induced module is nonzero and has vector-space basis the ordered monomials in negative current modes applied to the vacuum.

items.title: Mode translation descends to the affine vacuum module
items.statement: Prove that T(K)=0 and T(x_n)=-n x_(n-1) defines a derivation of the central extension preserving g[t], hence an operator on V^k(g) with T1=0 and [T,x_n]=-n x_(n-1).

items.title: Mutually local creative generators determine a state–field map
The universal affine vacuum module is restricted
items.statement: For every vector in V^k(g) and every x in g, sufficiently large positive current modes x_m annihilate that vector.

items.title: Affine current fields are local with the normalized current OPE
items.statement: On V^k(g), prove that J^x(z)=sum x_n z^(-n-1) is a field, is creative and translation-covariant, and satisfies [J^x(z),J^y(w)]=J^[x,y](w) delta(z,w)+kB(x,y) partial_w delta(z,w), hence the current OPE.

items.title: Universal affine vertex algebras exist at every complex level
items.statement: For finite-dimensional complex simple g with normalized invariant form and every k in C, V^k(g) has a unique vertex-algebra structure with vacuum 1 and generating current fields J^x(z); no noncritical-level or unitarity assumption is required for this vertex-algebra structure.

title: Vertex Algebra Axioms and State–Field Constructions: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Lower truncation alone does not imply locality
items.statement: Refute the claim that any two lower-truncated fields on a vector space are mutually local.

items.title: A commutative differential algebra gives a vertex algebra
items.statement: For V=C[u] with T=d/du and Y(a,z)b=(exp(zT)a)b, verify every state-field axiom, including lower truncation and locality.

items.title: The critical-level sl2 affine vertex algebra and its current OPE
items.statement: At normalized sl2 level k=-2, the universal affine vertex algebra exists and its e,f currents have OPE J^e(z)J^f(w)~J^h(w)/(z-w)-2/(z-w)^2, while the normalized Sugawara denominator vanishes.
